I have grown beans on this plot for many years using the seeds I save from each harvest, and they grow well enough without chemical fertilizer since beans make their own nitrogen in the soil. I will spread cow manure that my family collects to give the plants strength, but I cannot afford pesticides or irrigation for this small food plot. My grandchildren will do most of the planting, weeding, and harvesting, though I may hire a few young men from the village for a few days to help with the heavy work of breaking the soil at the start of the season.
